name: Bio-inspired small target motion detectors with feedback/prediction for tracking in clutter (Wang, Peng, Yue and coauthors)

inputs_state_output: Authors: input is the WHOLE grey-level frame (Vision Egg 500x250 at 1000 Hz synthetic; RIST 480x270 at 240 fps GoPro), processed by hand-designed, untrained retinotopic layers (Gaussian ommatidium blur, LMC temporal band-pass, four medulla channels with Gamma-kernel delays, STMD multiplicative correlation, lateral inhibition). State: (a) S1 apg-STMD keeps a 'memorizer' prediction map M(x,y,t) built by convolving STMD output with ring-shaped, direction-tuned prediction kernels (Eq. 20) and a leaky recursion F_t = conv(mu*E_t + (1-mu)*F_{t-dt}) (Eq. 21); M thresholds candidate areas where an attention kernel (min over orientation, max over scale, Eq. 4) adds contrast to the image (Eq. 5), and a decaying sum of past predictive gains is ADDED to the STMD output (facilitation, Eq. 23). (b) S2 Feedback STMD: STMD output delayed by a Gamma kernel and subtracted from medulla inputs (Eq. 9). (c) S3: a second subnetwork encodes background motion velocity/direction by neuronal ensemble coding and feeds a spatio-temporal feedback signal that suppresses and re-aligns medulla responses to background. (d) S4 vSTMD-F: previous-frame localisation output, Gaussian-smoothed, subtracted from ON/OFF potentials. Output: dense per-pixel STMD response maps (and preferred direction), thresholded into point detections; no boxes, no identities. Ours: bounded grey crop around the tracker prediction into stock/modernised FlyVis (trained, connectome-constrained, 721 columns, 34 output types), recurrent state carried over 4 exemplar + search frames, readout of 68 regional features per real detection region plus observed-target descriptor, 8 geometry and 6 assignment-context inputs. Key correspondence: our eye crop centred on the tracker prediction already plays the coarse role of their 'attention to predicted area'; what we do NOT have is (i) a facilitation gain carried in FlyVis state at the predicted target location, (ii) feedback from FlyVis output types back into earlier layers, (iii) explicit background-motion suppression inside the fly.
action_and_refusal: Authors: the output only changes which pixels are declared small-target detections at a threshold swept along an ROC curve; there is no box transfer, association, re-identification or track update, and no abstention option - the 'default' is simply a sub-threshold response. Prediction/feedback modulate the detection map, never override an external decision. Ours: full-box transfer of a selected real region into the track state before native ByteTrack matching, explicit 'unmatched' option and fixed no-action logit 0. Their work therefore gives no guidance on learning when to override the tracker's assignment; at most the facilitation map could act as a prior inside the fly that sharpens which real region is supported.
labels_and_loss: No training labels and no loss: all four systems are hand-tuned, learning-free (parameters in S1 Table I set from earlier analysis 'or experimentally', 'most remained identical for all test sequences'; S4 explicitly learning-free and names a learnable module as future work). Ground truth is used only for evaluation: a detection is a true positive if within 5 pixels of the annotated target centre (S1 Eq. 24-25). Class imbalance, neutral events and rare positive events are not handled because nothing is learned. Not informative for our MSE good-minus-harm objective problem.
data_camera_resolution_rate: Vision Egg: synthetic clips, single or 3-5 small targets (3x3 to ~15x15 px) on natural panorama backgrounds, controlled target/background velocity and luminance, 500x250 at 1000 Hz (S4 uses 470x310). RIST: real GoPro Hero 6 clips, 480x270 at 240 fps, one small moving target per video, camera ego-motion and bad weather present; reported counts differ across papers (16 videos in S2, 19 in S1 and S4 with 29,900 frames in S4, 21 in S3). Real-video evaluation in S1, S2, S3 uses only six 'randomly selected' RIST videos each (different six in S1 and S3); S4 reports mean over RIST and a cross-task XS-VID comparison. No train/test split (no training). Initial conditions: filters start from rest; facilitation needs a build-up period (S1 Fig. 14). Contrast with ours: BDD100K MOT, many large multi-class objects per frame, low annotation frame rate, real detector boxes, hundreds of videos with paired bootstrap - none of their datasets is MOT or has identity labels.
metrics_and_numbers: Authors' metrics are detection rate (true positives / actual targets) and false alarm rate (false positives per frame), shown as ROC curves; S4 adds mAUC/mAR/mAP/mF1 and orientation error AAE. S1: ROC curves only (Fig. 23 synthetic, Fig. 24 multi-target, Fig. 25 six RIST videos), detection rate equals 1 for target velocity 200-350 px/s at FA=1 (Fig. 23 text), stays >0.5 for oversize targets where baselines drop to 0; no table of numbers, no confidence intervals. S2: ROC curves (Fig. 14, Fig. 16 RIST); runtime Table III: ESTMD 0.064, DSTMD 0.116, Feedback STMD 0.084 s/frame (MATLAB CPU, 500x250 frames). S3: on 3-target synthetic video DR reaches 1 at FA=5, stated as +14 percentage points over time-delay feedback, +32 over ESTMD, +40 over DSTMD (Fig. 16(a) text); RIST: ROC curves on six videos (Fig. 17), no table. [uncertain: S4 numbers taken from an automatic summary, not read line by line] S4 (Table III/IV, RIST): vSTMD mF1 32.44, AAE 0.71 rad; vSTMD-F (feedback) mF1 39.33, AAE 0.50; Feedback STMD with delay tau 18.39 mF1; best natural baseline Frac-STMD mF1 24.88; the summary flagged internal text/table inconsistencies in S4 (e.g. 40% vs ~30% AAE reduction). None of these numbers can be translated into expected HOTA for our bench.
distinguishing_ablations: S1: qualitative with/without attention (Fig. 11-13, single row y0=190) and unfacilitated vs facilitated STMD (Fig. 14-18 primer-probe experiments, Fig. 19-21 occlusion on a circular path: facilitated response keeps spreading forward during occlusion while unfacilitated is ~0; carried response decays as occlusion angle and radius grow - prediction precision falls with longer occlusion). No quantitative ROC ablation of attention-only vs prediction-only on RIST was found in the text read. S2: with vs without delayed feedback - feedback shifts preferred velocity upward and suppresses slow background false positives but 'cannot directly affect the presence or absence' of tuning properties; parameter sensitivity over feedback gain alpha and Gamma order/time constant. S3: three-way comparison no feedback / time-delay feedback / spatio-temporal feedback on one synthetic scene (Fig. 14) - time-delay feedback weakens target and clutter alike and fails on fast background clutter; spatio-temporal feedback both suppresses and temporally misaligns background inputs; then ROC comparisons. S4: Table IV on RIST - feedback on vs off (mF1 32.44 -> 39.33), removal of Gaussian filter / cIDP / CDGC each degrades; instantaneous feedback beats delayed feedback. Mandatory components for the claimed effect: target velocity inside the STMD preferred band, target size within a few pixels, high frame rate so that Gamma delays correlate neighbouring pixels. Runs/seeds: deterministic hand-tuned models, single run, no variance, no significance tests; real-video ablations on six clips at most.
explanations_addressed: Lost discriminative/spatial information in readout: design analogy only - their output is a dense retinotopic map with a decaying positional prior rather than pooled regional features, suggesting the fly-side signal should keep a spatial, location-specific gain; no evidence about readouts. Target-vs-neighbour identification: caution - facilitation and attention boost WHATEVER lies at the predicted location and direction; nothing distinguishes the target from a similar neighbour at the same place, which is exactly our wrong-assignment failure; the background-feedback variants (S2-S4) suppress background clutter, not competing objects (the multi-target synthetic tests count detections, not identities). Training objective mismatched to final assignment: not addressed (no training). Rare useful events with high harm cost: not addressed. Insufficient history: direct but weak evidence on synthetic data - the memorizer/facilitation state carries a target prior through short occlusion and builds up over time (S1 Fig. 14, 19-21), with decay as occlusion lengthens; relevant to our temporal audit (only 14252 of 37296 queries have a supported prior query). Limits of the action: not addressed (no action).
evidence_strength: Weak for our decision. Peer-reviewed (IEEE TCYB, TNNLS, likely TIP) plus arXiv preprints, but one research lineage, shared backbone and datasets, no independent replication; evidence is ROC curves on synthetic scenes and six real single-target clips, single deterministic runs, no confidence intervals; an open Python STMD library exists (repository README verified, implementation files not inspected); S4 summary reports text/table inconsistencies. Regime (tiny targets, 240-1000 Hz) is far from BDD100K MOT.
difference_from_tried: Differs in locus: our tried mechanisms (fixed/learned association of 3 D peaks, ridge target model on 4 exemplars, per-action MSE good-minus-harm head with softmax threshold, category replacement, context features) all act in the readout/decision after FlyVis. The STMD feedback/prediction mechanisms act INSIDE the visual model: a positional facilitation gain integrated over time and added to the response (S1), and negative feedback of delayed output or of a background-motion estimate onto earlier layers (S2-S4). Partial overlap: our eye crop is already centred on the tracker's Kalman prediction, so the 'attend to the predicted area' part is already present coarsely; the ridge target model provides static appearance, not a decaying positional prior. Not different in one key respect: the prediction is a constant-velocity motion prior like ByteTrack's Kalman filter, so any gain must come from expressing it inside the fly dynamics rather than from new information.
candidate_node_change: Node: FlyVis STATE (and optionally input preparation). Change 'predictive facilitation': keep a per-column facilitation map F carried across search frames, F_t = leaky integration of the fly's own output-type activity at the previously supported target location, shifted by the target's last displacement within the eye and spread by a ring/Gaussian kernel (S1 Eq. 20-23), and add beta*F to the selected output types' activity (or as a small multiplicative input gain on the crop, S1 Eq. 5) before the regional readout. Problem it addresses: FlyVis state on search frames updates without any target-specific memory (history insufficient, regional features do not encode 'where the target was'), so correct and neighbouring regions receive similar activity. Second, more expensive option: a delayed negative feedback edge from output types to medulla inputs (S2) to suppress background, which requires retraining the 734-parameter model and is lower priority because detector boxes already remove most background clutter. Equal controls: old D readout on unmodified features; stock C FlyVis; eye input R1 (same facilitation applied to raw crop intensities); no-fly geometry control (the same shifted Gaussian prior applied directly to region geometry/Kalman distance) - required, because the prior is a motion prior the tracker already has. Cheap CPU check on saved data: on the 553 wrong baseline assignments with the correct high-confidence detection inside the eye (and on the 14252 queries with a supported prior query), approximate facilitation by adding the decayed previous-query regional features of the supported region (aligned by region overlap) to current regional features and measure the rank-1 rate of the correct region among candidate regions with the existing fixed readout, versus the no-fly geometry prior with matched strength. Proceed to GPU (recompute FlyVis maps with facilitation inside the state on train26 and then val) only if the fly-feature facilitation beats the no-fly geometry prior on correct-region rank-1 with a paired bootstrap lower bound above zero, and the oracle reserve restricted to rescued cases is not already explained by geometry; otherwise stop.
strongest_objection: The mechanism is a hand-tuned constant-velocity spatial prior validated on tiny single targets at 240-1000 Hz with ROC curves on six clips; it adds no information the Kalman prediction and eye centring do not already contain, and by construction it boosts whatever object occupies the predicted place - including the wrong neighbour that causes our wrong assignments - so it is more likely to reinforce the baseline choice than to find the 48+58+553 fixable cases. Its benefit in their papers comes from suppressing pixel-level background false alarms, a failure mode our detector-region readout largely does not have.
cost_and_hardware: CPU check on saved regional features and query histories: a few hours, no new FlyVis maps. GPU stage: new FlyVis maps with facilitation in state on one 12 GB GPU, comparable to a previous map-generation run over train26 + val (hours, within single-CUDA-process rule). Feedback-edge variant needs FlyVis retraining on the flow task (ensemble members) - expensive, not justified by this evidence.
